The USA, 1954–75: Conflict at Home and Abroad
KT1: The Civil Rights Movement, 1954–60
Cues & Questions (Left)
Notes (Right - Student to Fill In)
KT1.1: Position of Black Americans in early 1950s
Describe segregation and the 'Jim Crow' laws in the South.
What were the roles of the NAACP and CORE?
KT1.2: Developments in Education
Brown v. Topeka (1954):
What were the causes and the significance of the ruling?
Little Rock High School (1957):
Key events and the role of President Eisenhower.
KT1.3: Montgomery Bus Boycott (1955-60)
Causes: Why did the boycott start? (Rosa Parks).
Success: Why was it successful? Consider the Supreme Court and MLK's leadership.
Impact: Significance of the SCLC and the 1957 Civil Rights Act.
KT1.4: Opposition to Civil Rights
The KKK: Methods and the murder of Emmett Till (1955).
Political opposition: White Citizens' Councils and the 'Dixiecrats'.
KT2: Civil Rights Progress, 1960–75
Cues & Questions (Left)
Notes (Right - Student to Fill In)
KT2.1: Progress 1960-62
Greensboro Sit-ins (1960): Significance of student-led protest.
Freedom Riders (1961): Key features and the Anniston bomb.
James Meredith (1962): How did he challenge the University of Mississippi?
KT2.2: Peaceful Protests 1963-65
Birmingham (1963) & March on Washington: Impact of 'I Have a Dream'.
Freedom Summer (1964): Mississippi murders and voter registration.
Selma (1965): Events and the 1965 Voting Rights Act.
KT2.3: Malcolm X and Black Power
Malcolm X: Nation of Islam beliefs vs. his later views.
Black Power: Stokely Carmichael and the 1968 Mexico Olympics.
Black Panther Movement: Methods and achievements.
KT2.4: Civil Rights 1965-75
Riots of 1965-67: Causes and the findings of the Kerner Report.
MLK in the North: Successes and failures. Assassination impact.
KT3: US Involvement in Vietnam, 1954–68
Cues & Questions (Left)
Notes (Right - Student to Fill In)
KT3.1: Reasons for Involvement (1954-63)
Dien Bien Phu: End of French rule and the division of Vietnam.
Eisenhower: Domino Theory and the weaknesses of the Diem gov.
Kennedy: Overthrow of Diem and the Strategic Hamlet Program.
KT3.2: Escalation under Johnson
Gulf of Tonkin Incident (1964): How did this lead to full war?
KT3.3: Nature of Conflict (1964-68)
Vietcong: Guerilla tactics (tunnels, booby traps, Ho Chi Minh trail).
USA: Search & Destroy, Operation Rolling Thunder, Chemical weapons.
Tet Offensive (1968): Key features and why it was a turning point.
KT4: Ending the Conflict in Vietnam, 1969–75
Cues & Questions (Left)
Notes (Right - Student to Fill In)
KT4.1: Opposition to the War
Why did opposition grow? (TV coverage, draft system, students).
My Lai Massacre (1968) and Kent State (1970): Public reaction.
KT4.2: Support for the War
Fear of Communism and the 'Silent Majority'.
KT4.3: The Peace Process
Nixon: Vietnamisation, the Nixon Doctrine, and Kissinger's role.
Attacks on Cambodia (1970) and Laos (1971).
Paris Peace Agreement (1973) and the cost of the war.
KT4.4: Failure in Vietnam
Strengths of NV: Russian/Chinese support and tactics.
US Weaknesses: Morale, failed tactics, and domestic opposition.
